incident: Ryuk Speed Run, 2 Hours to Ransom

sources.title: Ryuk Speed Run, 2 Hours to Ransom - The DFIR Report

narrative_before: A phishing email linked to a Google Docs page offered a 'report' that was actually a Bazar Loader executable (Report-Review20-10.exe); execution needed user interaction. The DFIR Report states 'the time from initial Bazar execution to domain recon was 5 minutes' and Cobalt Strike was deployed within 10 minutes. The actors Kerberoasted with Rubeus and used Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) to obtain domain admin, then used RDP from the beachhead to two domain controllers and SMB (ADMIN$ service execution) to backup, file and deployment servers. Ryuk 'was deployed in 2 hours with the actor completing all objectives in 3 hours', starting with backup systems and file servers. Discovery output was exfiltrated via FTP.

machines.name: dc
machines.role: domain controller (Cobalt Strike, AD module, Zerologon)

machines.name: srv_backup
machines.role: backup server (Veeam services stopped, encrypted first)

detection_moments.description: Beachhead Cobalt Strike beacon within 10 minutes, then RDP to both domain controllers with CS executables dropped.
detection_moments.evidence: 'the time from initial Bazar execution to domain recon was 5 minutes'; Cobalt Strike on DCs around 1 hour (Ryuk Speed Run, The DFIR Report)

detection_moments.description: Zerologon + Rubeus Kerberoast yield domain admin; AdFind/Rubeus output exfiltrated via FTP before ransom staging.
detection_moments.evidence: Rubeus Kerberoast and Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472); 'Discovery data (AdFind and Rubeus outputs) was exfiltrated out of the network via FTP'

attack_path: phishing link -> Bazar Loader Report-Review20-10.exe run by user; injects svchost.exe (T1566.002/T1204/T1055)
RDP from beachhead to domain controller; Cobalt Strike executable dropped; Zerologon privesc (T1021.001/T1068)
RDP to second domain controller; Cobalt Strike deployed (T1021.001)
SMB to ADMIN$ share, executable run as a service (T1021.002/T1569.002)
Ryuk deployed over RDP from DCs to file servers and workstations (T1486)
ambiguities: No real hostnames in report; machine names are role-derived.
Report does not describe how/when defenders detected the intrusion; detection moments modelled on beacon/lateral and privesc+exfil stages.
Exact encrypted host count not given.
